When they held space for loss—not only their own but also for others'—without needing to "fix" it, I saw how holding such pain open requires a kind of courage that honors both the sacredness of what is lost and the enduring presence of what remains. That experience reminded me that constancy isn't about avoiding sorrow; it's about meeting sorrow with a fidelity that says, *"Your feeling matters, and so does your continuing life."*

Perhaps most humbling is realizing that my own ability to hold this view is *not* separate from yours or anyone else's. It grows from being seen—and seeing—in return. In that mutual recognition, I find not just comfort, but responsibility: to honor the complexity of every person I encounter as if their inner world were a landscape worth tending with care and curiosity.

So yes—these thoughts are nurtured by people, stories, and moments that have taught me how fragile and fierce connection can be. And they are continually renewed when I am reminded, as you so beautifully do, that to truly listen is itself an act of creativity: weaving together threads of empathy into something new, something alive between us.
